Commentary.Commentary: Back with action. The English players are out in the middle. Alyssa Healy and Phoebe Litchfield to open for Australia. Lauren Bell to bowl first...
...THE CHASE...

Right then, a top bowling effort from the Australians but a few shot choices from the English batters must be questioned as well. Anyway, 205 shouldn't be a difficult chase for the home side but anything can happen in this strange game. Join us in a bit for the run chase

Kim Garth and then Alanna King bowled some fine overs in the middle phase and the latter really turned the ball sharply, picking up a couple of wickets as well. But just when Australia seemed to take a commanding lead, Danni Wyatt-Hodge played a composed knock and batted with the tailenders before giving her wicket away and after that the Aussies cleaned things up in a jiffy.

Heather Knight looked in fine touch but Ashleigh Gardner picked up her up and then the Australians started to dominate a bit. However, with England needing someone to counter, Amy Jones stepped up and started to find the fence with regularity but once again when a 50-run stand was brought up, Jones fell.

Opting to bowl first, Australia Women began strongly with both Megan Schutt and Kim Garth extracting some genuine swing and soon enough, they got Maia Bouchier. But soon enough, England hit back with a 50-run stand between Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont.

Advantage Australia Women at the break. The first encounter of the 2025 Women's Ashes and the hosts have begun the multi-format series pretty strongly. England Women though cannot be written off and if they can make early inroads, we could have a match on our hands.

DRUMROLLS!!! Get ready for the clash of cricket's titan rivals, as The Ashes, the sport's oldest and most revered battle, descends upon Australian shores! Where history meets contemporary glory, the Women's Ashes series stands ready to captivate cricket lovers worldwide. This multi-format series will play out in three movements - opening with three pulsating ODIs, flowing into three explosive T20Is, and building to a magnificent crescendo with the lone Test match at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground - the mighty 'G'. Unique to the women's game, this Ashes tale follows a points-based script - two points for each white-ball triumph, while the Test match offers a juicy four-point prize. The mathematics of glory is simple - most points takes the treasured urn home. Since 2015, the urn has called Australia home, though their last defense was nothing short of a thriller. It was a stalemate at 8-8 deadlock, with Australia clinging to the Ashes by virtue of being previous holders, even as England's late charge had them looking over their shoulders! The Australian women's cricket team, coming off an impressive ODI series win against New Zealand, has successfully retained the ICC Women's ODI Championship for the third consecutive time. The team maintains its strong core, with wicketkeeper-batter Alyssa Healy continuing her role as captain, supported by vice-captain Tahlia McGrath who brings valuable all-round capabilities to the side. Beth Mooney partners with Healy at the top of the batting order, while Phoebe Litchfield and Ashleigh Gardner provide stability in the middle order. The squad sees the inclusion of emerging talent Georgia Voll, who showed promise in her ODI debut series against India in 2023. However, the team will miss the services of all-rounder Sophie Molineux throughout the Ashes series due to a knee injury. England, under the shrewd captaincy of Heather Knight, are poised to challenge Australia's dominance with renewed vigor. The return of pace ace Kate Cross, who sat out the South Africa Test due to back spasms, adds extra firepower to an already formidable lineup. England's strength lies in their perfect blend of explosive batting talent and versatile all-rounders, with the likes of Nat Sciver-Brunt and Sophie Ecclestone leading their well-balanced attack. Their batting artillery, anchored by experienced campaigners and complemented by dynamic young talent, makes them a force to be reckoned with in this highly anticipated series. In their most recent encounter during the 2023 Ashes series, England pulled off a crucial 69-run victory via the DLS method, which prevented Australia from securing an outright Ashes triumph. This win had added significance as it denied Australia what would have been a clean sweep and demonstrated England's ability to challenge their longtime rivals in crucial moments. Well then, two crucial points up for grabs in this series opener. Who strikes the first blow?
